page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ebmc6.26xlarge is a bare-metal compute-oriented instance within the ECS Bare Metal family. It provides 104 dedicated vCPUs built on the x86_64 architecture and operates under a KVM hypervisor foundation. The server delivers 192.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 1.85 GB of RAM per vCPU core. It does not include integrated local disk storage, nor does it feature discrete GPU acceleration hardware.

Networking capability is anchored by a baseline bandwidth of 32 Gbps, enabling rapid data movement across distributed environments. Storage operations rely entirely on attached remote cloud storage services due to the absence of onboard disks. In terms of resource allocation, the high core-to-memory ratio prioritizes multi-threaded computational throughput over heavy in-memory data capacity. This bare-metal architecture delivers dedicated CPU tenancy without virtualization overhead, offering qualitative cost efficiency for compute-heavy parallel workloads that can maximize high core occupancy.

The compute-focused configuration makes the ecs.ebmc6.26xlarge suitable for CPU-bound batch processing, high-throughput distributed compilation, continuous integration pipelines, video transcoding, scientific numerical processing, and compute-intensive microservices that rely on networked storage backends.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ebmc6.26xlarge is a dedicated bare-metal instance within the ECS Bare Metal family, engineered for compute-heavy enterprise workloads. It features 104 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs and 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 1.85 GB of RAM per core. Operating on a KVM hypervisor architecture, the instance contains no local storage volumes and no discrete GPU accelerators, necessitating remote block storage attachments for persistent state management. A 32 Gbps baseline network bandwidth supports high-throughput distributed communication. By eliminating hypervisor overhead and delivering high core density relative to memory, the ecs.ebmc6.26xlarge achieves strong resource efficiency for highly parallelized processing tasks. Tradeoffs include complete reliance on networked storage for all I/O operations and limited memory headroom for memory-dense datasets. The server fits high-throughput compute workloads such as parallel compilation, CI/CD runners, batch processing, and compute-intensive microservices.
